strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing genuine limitations of CVaR-PG (sample inefficiency, blindness to success, vanishing gradients with flat-tailed returns)
Solid theoretical contributions including new Bellman operator for VaR with contraction mapping properties and recovery of Markovian policies via cumulative reward tracking
Consistent empirical improvements across three test domains, with particularly clear benefits in Maze where CVaR-PG fails
Comprehensive baseline comparisons (CVaR-PG, PCVaR-PG, RET-CAP, MIX) with fair on-policy implementation
Principled handling of practical challenges (quantile crossing) with softplus-based monotonicity enforcement
Clear problem motivation and intuitive core idea grounded in CVaR's relationship to quantiles
weaknesses: Critical convergence gap: convergence properties under iterative updates from arbitrary initialization remain unknown; Proposition 3.4 only shows π* maximizes objective under corresponding value function, not during optimization
Theory-practice mismatch: theoretical results require ε=0, κ=0, but practical algorithm uses soft loss with ε,κ>0; applicability of theory to implementation unclear
Artificial experimental domains designed specifically to have verifiable risk-averse behavior; authors acknowledge environment design is itself a nontrivial problem; limited generalization assessment

Hyperparameter sensitivity and tuning burden: trade-off parameter ω is crucial but no ablation studies provided; domain-specific decay schedules suggest sensitivity without principled selection guidance
Incremental improvements over RET-CAP in some domains (LunarLander: 'slightly higher'); gains not consistently substantial despite added complexity
Missing ablation studies: no analysis of CVaR-PG (g₁) vs VaR-PG (g₂) component contributions; no failure mode analysis; limited investigation of when method excels
Experimental design concerns: implementations differ from original papers (on-policy without IS), only 10 seeds, no statistical significance tests; harder to assess true improvements
Limited algorithmic novelty: VaR Bellman operator closely follows Hau et al. (2025); main contribution is combination rather than novel components
Reproducibility limitations: domain-specific hyperparameters (ω decay schedules), no code mentioned, non-standard implementation choices
Presentation could be clearer: dense notation in Section 3.2, relationship between Algorithms 2-3 unclear, interaction of gradient terms g₁ and g₂ not deeply analyzed

strengths: Clear and intuitive motivation: identifies specific CVaR-PG limitations (sample waste, blindness to success) and proposes a principled solution leveraging CVaR=E[VaR] relationship
Solid theoretical framework for VaR: Propositions 3.1-3.2 rigorously establish VaR Bellman operator as contraction with unique fixed point; extension to random rewards (Appendix A.2) is thorough
Novel Markovian policy adaptation: Propositions 3.3-3.4 showing recovery of optimal VaR policies via quantile value functions with cumulative reward tracking is technically interesting
Consistent empirical improvements: CVaR-VaR outperforms baselines on CVaR metrics across tested domains; multi-step advantage estimation implementation is solid
Transparent presentation and honest limitations: Detailed proofs, explicit hyperparameters, acknowledgment of convergence gap, clear exclusion rationale for some domains/baselines
weaknesses: Critical convergence gap: Paper explicitly states 'it remains an open question whether iterative updates starting from arbitrary π̄ and v will converge to π̄*'. The practical algorithm (Eq. 11) lacks theoretical convergence guarantees; only empirical validation provided. For a top-tier venue, this is a fundamental weakness

Weak theoretical justification for combined objective: Eq. 7 is mathematically invariant in ω since CVaR_α ≡ E_β~U[0,α][VaR_β]. Paper doesn't explain why combination improves optimization—benefit must come from landscape/convergence properties, but this isn't analyzed. Decay of ω to 0 suggests VaR is auxiliary

Severely limited experimental validation: Only 3 domains, all heavily modified; authors explicitly excluded Ant/HalfCheetah because defining 'practically relevant risk-averse objectives is itself a nontrivial research problem'; no real-world applications; eliminates major claim to practical impact

Modest empirical improvements with confounded comparisons: Improvements over RET-CAP (closest baseline) are marginal (Maze: both ~0.95, LunarLander: CVaR ~200 vs ~150, Pendulum: comparable risk metrics); substantial error bar overlap in Fig. 3e; standard on-policy implementations differ from original papers, undermining direct comparison

Missing design justifications and ablations: ω decay schedules vary across domains (40% vs 25%) without principled justification; no ablation separating VaR-PG from multi-step advantage; sensitivity to quantile discretization (I) not analyzed; quantile crossing mitigation not validated

Unclear algorithm-theory connection: Propositions 3.3-3.4 require *optimal* quantile functions to establish correctness, but don't address convergence from arbitrary initialization (the actual learning scenario). Theory and Algorithm 4 operate at different levels; which guarantees apply where is ambiguous

Incomplete handling of practical details: Eq. 12 produces α_t that may not lie in discretized set Λ; projection step mentioned but effect on convergence not analyzed; computing α_t requires evaluating v(s',β) for all β ∈ Λ (computational cost not discussed); multi-step advantage uses trajectory-determined α values with unclear theoretical implications

strengths: Well-motivated approach leveraging the observation that CVaR equals expectation of tail quantiles, addressing real limitations of CVaR-PG (sample inefficiency, blindness to success, vanishing gradients)
Technically sound theoretical contributions with rigorous derivation of new VaR Bellman operator (Eq. 8) and clear proofs of contraction properties and fixed points (Propositions 3.1-3.2)
Elegant connection showing how to recover optimal VaR policies from Markovian policies via cumulative reward tracking (Proposition 3.3), enabling practical learning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple domains, metrics, baselines, 10 random seeds with error bars, and honest discussion of domain limitations
Complete implementation details with clear algorithms, network architectures, hyperparameters, and practical design choices (monotonicity enforcement via softplus, multi-step advantage estimation)
Transparent about limitations and open questions, particularly regarding convergence of the Markovian policy learning algorithm
weaknesses: Critical theoretical gap: Proposition 3.4 characterizes π̄* as maximizing Eq. 11 under its own value function, but the paper explicitly states convergence from arbitrary initialization remains an open question. Algorithm 4 performs iterative updates without convergence guarantees, creating significant theory-practice mismatch

Trade-off parameter ω behavior poorly understood: no principled guidance for setting ω, no sensitivity analysis provided, and scheduling (decay from 0.5 to 0) appears ad-hoc. Unclear why ω is needed if VaR-PG is superior, and stated justification (controlling tail beyond one quantile) lacks empirical validation

Severely limited experimental scope: only three custom-modified domains with artificially-injected risky regions; paper acknowledges designing meaningful risk-averse objectives is unsolved; standard environments excluded due to design issues; no standard risk-averse benchmarks tested; questionable generalizability

Comparison fairness concerns: implementations differ from original papers (no off-policy importance sampling except MIX), affecting validity of baseline comparisons; PCVaR-PG failure possibly due to experimental setup rather than algorithmic issues; unclear if multi-step advantage estimation helps baselines equally

Limited novelty: the Bellman operator is a straightforward adaptation of Hau et al. (2025) to state-only functions; main contribution is combining existing techniques (CVaR-PG + quantile regression) rather than fundamental innovation; heavy dependence on very recent concurrent work

Missing critical ablations: no isolation of VaR contribution (e.g., setting ω=1 throughout), no sensitivity analysis for ω parameter, unclear which component drives improvements per domain, no comparison with VaR-PG alone despite theoretical motivation

Insufficient insight into method success/failure: Limited explanation for why RET-CAP is inconsistent in Maze beyond CVaR-PG's vanishing gradients; improvements are incremental in LunarLander/Pendulum vs. dramatic in Maze; no analysis of what environmental properties favor CVaR-VaR

Technical details underspecified: Algorithm 4's handling of quantile selection when no β satisfies constraint (numerical stability); Equation 8's order of operations (max before/after expectation) unclear; quantile discretization parameters (I, ε) untested for sensitivity; proj(α, Λ) implementation unspecified
